# Native mean property regression fixtures

These are compact synthetic regression artifacts, generated by
`tests/emit_mean_property_fixtures.py` and
`tests/emit_density_property_fixtures.py` from the public
`YE3TRepresentation → Basis → LinearModel` workflow in `ye3t-methods`.
Targets are generated from known coefficients and fitted back with ridge;
the models are not material-property estimates. Raw fit attempts and broader
LAMMPS evidence are under
`ye3t-workflows/MLIP/standardization_p6_cpu_20261006`.

The fixture cases separately test selected tag counts 0, 1, and 2. The
tag-2 case uses an exact compiler `edge_marginal` schedule, a partial-periodic
cell, and repeated images of the same base atom. Each fixture stores directed
edge occurrences and Python fitted means for C++ parity. The artifact reader
checks canonical model, compiler-source, schedule and plan hashes before
evaluation. The fixtures also include rotated vectors and the independently
transformed Cartesian vector/tensor means; native tests check rotation,
inversion parity, and neighbor-order invariance. Separate cases exercise an
L2 source channel, two chemical species, and an isolated center in the
LAMMPS integration driver. The uneven case has one, two, and one neighbor
occurrences across its three owned centers. The pure tag-2 one-neighbor case
fits on the periodic environment, then evaluates with only one distinct
neighbor and verifies that the mean is zero.
The rank-3 L1 tag-2 case has a nontrivial internal Young block
``κ=(2,1)`` with a nonzero fitted coefficient and a globally symmetric
parent; it exercises the saved edge-marginal schedule on CPU and in the
tagged CPU/device parity driver.

The `density_*` cases test ordinary-density full-M L1 and L2
models with PACE radial channels. They cover two chemical species, an L2
angular source, repeated periodic occurrences, and a rank-3 repeated-content
multipath case with 26 selected features. Their v2 native plans
and stored Python reference rows support native parity checks. The CPU LAMMPS
property compute reads these v2 density artifacts. The standalone and
single/two-rank integration tests include all three cases; the Kokkos device
compute does not yet accept density artifacts.
